text:
on man's penchant for total self-destruction

always notable to me how a man has one thing go wrong, then it inevitably kicks off a death spiral

which accelerates into BITFD mode, burn it the fuck down

and the spiral only ends, when everything is gone.

1/5

this is also known as "rock bottom"

u cannot lose more. u legitimately have nothing more left to lose.

this also happens to be the short answer to, "I know someone spiraling towards rock bottom, what can I do"

nothing

be there for them when they hit bottom

until then, get out of the way. there is a process in motion that the rest of the world is powerless to stop.

2/5

the way I was thinking about this, is that a man is a city

each building represents some facet of his life

job, family, money, shit like that

one building falls. 

we'll say he gets wiped out financially, some stablecoin or dumbass crypto trade.

he's stunned, hasn't told anyone.

the issue is less the building, and more the loss of that buildings' relationship to all the other buildings in the city.

interdependency problem

3/5

having no money causes tension and suffering from attachment, the Buddhist dukkha, because your persona, your "role" that you are in the other buildings has been impacted.

maybe he was known as a big swinger, wealthy, successful, cars, clubs, women

that's problematic

can you rebuild the downed building immediately? no, not an option, or at least not one which would restore his prior identities to 100%

so this attachment to these identities -- which are clearly unsustainable -- is going to be a source of everpresent pain and misery.

4/5

this is where "burn it all the fuck down" quietly enters the stage as a potential option.

it is a lever to be pulled once the pain becomes too intense.

you can see how he'd get there.

to resolve the tension, either the old building must go up, or the rest of the buildings must come down...period.

a man can be wealthy. a man can be broke. 

a man cannot be trapped in this phantasmagoria of bothness, between two semi-coherent yet nonexistent versions of himself.

he needs a new persona, new identity, needs to let the old "him" burn to the ground.

5/5

the much cleaner alternative is to just tell the world that he is officially dead-ass broke. men are simply too proud -- they'll never voluntarily choose this path.

would it solve all these problems, yes

but in doing so, there are so many interconnected identities, so many layers of shifting perception that he'd have to deal with along the way, a long road and an enormously painful one

people squawking the whole time, "did you hear he's getting evicted," "his lady left and took the kids," 

also, now that I think about it...it would not solve his problems at all.

it aligns his self-image (broke) with the world's perception of him. 

however, it doesn't signal an end...all it would do is begin the process of the other buildings being lowered or removed.

END: bad and worse

it also begins the public societal torture.

play by play humilitation

slow and drawn out, probably as painful as one could draw it up.

just a weak man getting vulture'd by his bad decisions, watching his old identity get dismantled bit by bit.

like choosing a voluntary pillory in the town square. 

the picture I am painting here, reality is probably 100x more painful, and there are 100x the elements to this that I haven't thought of.

so, burning it all down may go beyond pride. it may actually be the rational decision.

mostly because, the alternative is way worse than it seemed at first

you are going to lose a tremendous amount in both scenarios

neither seem to have significant moral/ethical upside or downside, screwed both ways

"I told the world the truth about myself" is not always wise, honest, or honorable, or at best its neutral. 
 
and for all we know, the slow road could take years, where you're in severe and glaringly public pain the entire time

or?

you can roll the dice with complete and total self-destruction

you self-immolate, and emerge as an identity yet to be determined.

I don't know which choice is "correct" - I just know which I've seen play out over and over.

**not investment advice
